correctness.rationale: For each finite N>=2 and all kappa>0 the joint two-bath-state exclusion chain is irreducible. Fixed-bath means and pair covariances solve the exact harmonic two-particle Dirichlet system, including the adjacent-pair source. Singular stationary equations prove the weak-bath mixture and rapid-bath averaging with explicit normalized covariances, yielding strictly opposite pair signs. Continuity supplies at least one zero for every pair, without asserting uniqueness for N>2. The N=2 mixed-moment equations reproduce the exact rational expression with sole positive root sqrt(10)/2-1. Standalone verify.py passed exact symbolic and independently constructed full generator checks at N=2..5 plus static moment identities at N=2..80. Finite checks support rather than prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The finite-chain sign of connected correlations in an SSEP is a well motivated structural observable. Fixed reservoirs produce long-range anticorrelation, whereas slow common switching of one reservoir generates an explicit strictly positive intersite covariance even with unchanged mean density; all pairs reverse sign relative to rapid switching. This separates external common-noise fluctuations from exclusion anticorrelations, establishes a complete all-size qualitative phase transition, and provides a quantitative two-site rate for physical and numerical benchmarks. It is not merely renaming or recomputing the classical fixed-bath formula.
